name: Dick Durbin
role: U.S. Senator from Illinois (1997–present); Senate Democratic Whip
summary: Longtime Illinois Democrat and Senate Democratic leader who backs expanded health coverage, labor rights, gun limits, abortion and LGBTQ rights, and a path to legal status for undocumented immigrants who came as children. He opposes the death penalty and the 2002 Iraq war authorization, and has stressed Congress's war powers and constitutional checks on executive power.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Voted for the 2009 Affordable Care Act and which extended coverage toward everyone.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Voted repeatedly (1999, 2000, 2005) for amendments raising the federal minimum wage.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Condemned giving the top 0.1 percent a $400,000 yearly tax cut while minimum-wage workers get $20 a month, calling it indefensible.

unions-good.rationale: Said the labor movement created the middle class in America and backed the Employee Free Choice Act as a union organizer's tool.

limit-guns.rationale: Voted for gun-show background checks, safe-storage and handgun safety measures in 1998-2000.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted yes on cloture and passage of the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act repealing the Defense of Marriage Act.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted against the 1997 ban on partial-birth abortions and for amendments to repeal limits on abortions in military facilities and federal health plans.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Author of the DREAM Act, who has told Dreamers' stories on the floor 146 times and defends TPS holders, pressing for legal status rather than tight restriction.

nation-first.rationale: Condemned Trump's questioning of long-standing alliances and his senseless tariffs, saying the global economic order brought unparalleled prosperity to Americans.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called for bringing the Warner-Lieberman cap-and-trade climate bill to the floor, against a Republican filibuster.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted in 2001 for amendments to preserve the estate tax against repeal.

separate-church-state.rationale: Opposed the DeMint amendment on religious-school building aid, saying the Senate was honoring the Constitution's establishment clause.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Said Trump undermined the bedrock principle that sovereign borders will be respected by laying claim to Greenland, the Panama Canal and Canada.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Stated that he concurs that President Truman was right to recognise Israel's right to exist and called its creation after the Holocaust almost inevitable.

school-vouchers.rationale: Voted no in 2001 on an amendment for low-income school choice funding.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted yes in 2001, 2003 and 2008 on measures for an economic stimulus package, including the 2008 stimulus bill.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Backed the Paycheck Fairness Act to stop employers paying women less because they believe women's work is worth less, and said women are not getting a fair deal.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Co-sponsors and chaired the first Senate Judiciary hearing on the Equality Act, which extends civil rights protections equally.

separated-powers.rationale: Insists the Constitution's Article I gives war powers to Congress and supports Congress checking a president's war-making.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Denounced leaders who discarded the rule of law after 9/11 by turning to torture, indefinite detention and makeshift Guantanamo tribunals.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Voted yes in 1998 on the accession of Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to the North Atlantic Treaty.

death-penalty.rationale: Announced 15 years ago that he can no longer support the death penalty and argues it is applied to the poor, Black Americans and the possibly innocent.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Said that investing in family planning and sex education produces fewer unplanned pregnancies and fewer abortions.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Called for a viable path to a two-state solution in Gaza and the region, which involves territorial compromise for peace.

collective-defense.rationale: Introduced the Baltic Defense and Deterrence Act to deter Russia from forcing NATO to invoke its Article 5 collective-security commitment.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted no in 2009 on amendments to end TARP bailout spending and to bar bailouts for auto manufacturers.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Co-sponsors the Equality Act and held its first Senate Judiciary hearing as chair, which expands civil rights protections for LGBTQ+ Americans.

harassment-claims-court-access.rationale: Criticised a nominee for testifying against the bipartisan law ending forced arbitration of workplace sexual assault and harassment claims.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted no in 1997 on the balanced budget constitutional amendment.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Cited the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant for Putin over atrocities in Ukraine approvingly, as a reason he cannot travel freely.

shut-down-tax-havens.rationale: Pressed a Treasury nominee to close loopholes and raise taxes on those who avoid tax through offshore tax havens.

torture-always-illegal.rationale: Denounced torture as one of the steps by which leaders discarded the rule of law after 9/11.
